lemon-chickpea-salad: Whisk the olive oil and lemon juice in a large bowl. Add a few grinds of black pepper.
Add the drained chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes and parsley. Toss until everything is lightly coated.
Fold in the feta. Taste before adding salt: feta and canned chickpeas can already be salty. Divide into portions and serve.
lemon-white-bean-skillet: Warm the oil in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and stir for about 1 minute, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the beans, water and oregano. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for about 5 minutes. Mash a spoonful of beans against the pan to thicken the sauce.
Add the spinach in handfuls and stir until wilted. If the pan looks dry, add another splash of water.
Remove from the heat, stir in lemon juice, then taste and season. Divide into portions and serve with bread.
blueberry-overnight-oats: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt and optional cinnamon in a clean covered container.
Cover and place in the refrigerator overnight so the oats soften. Do not leave the mixture on the counter.
Stir, adding a splash of milk if you prefer a looser texture. Top with blueberries and freshly sliced banana, then serve.
crispy-sheet-pan-gnocchi: Heat the oven and prep pan.
Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Add the uncooked gnocchi, whole cherry tomatoes, and smashed garlic cloves directly onto the pan. Drizzle with olive oil, oregano, salt, and black pepper. Toss with hands until evenly glossy, spreading in a single layer.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, tossing once halfway through, until gnocchi are deeply golden and crisp on the edges and tomatoes have burst and released juices.
Toss in the torn basil right on the hot sheet so it wilts slightly. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan and serve hot straight from the pan.
mediterranean-warm-green-lentils: Heat olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add chopped shallot and cook 3 minutes until translucent. Stir in minced garlic, cumin, and coriander for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the drained lentils and 2 tablespoons of water or broth. Simmer gently for 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until hot throughout.
Stir in the spinach leaves in batches until just wilted (about 1 minute). Remove pan from heat and stir in lemon juice, lemon zest, salt, and pepper.
Transfer to warm bowls. Scatter crumbled goat cheese or feta over top and finish with a light drizzle of olive oil.
smashed-cucumber-edamame-bowl: Place cucumbers on a cutting board. Use the flat side of a heavy chef knife or rolling pin to firmly smack them until split lengthwise. Cut diagonally into bite-sized jagged pieces.
In a small bowl, whisk together tamari, toasted sesame oil, rice vinegar, grated ginger, and maple syrup until emulsified.
In a mixing bowl, toss smashed cucumbers, thawed edamame, and sliced scallions with the vinaigrette until well coated.
Gently fold in diced avocado so it stays intact. Divide into portions, scatter toasted sesame seeds over top, and serve immediately.
garlic-butter-bean-mushroom-toast: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sliced mushrooms in a single layer without moving for 3 minutes until deeply browned, then stir and cook 2 minutes more.
Turn heat down to medium. Add grated garlic and thyme; stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the drained cannellini beans and stock. Bring to a simmer for 4 minutes. Lightly crush about one third of the beans with the back of a fork to create a creamy sauce.
Toast the sourdough slices until deeply golden. Stir white wine vinegar, salt, and pepper into the beans. Spoon generously over hot toast and garnish with chopped chives.
spiced-apple-cinnamon-porridge: Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add diced apple and ½ tsp of the cinnamon. Cook for 3–4 minutes until apple starts to soften slightly at edges.
Add oats, water, milk, remaining ½ tsp cinnamon, nutmeg, and a pinch of salt to the saucepan. Stir well and bring to a gentle bubble.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring frequently, for 10–12 minutes until oats are tender and porridge is thick and creamy. (5 minutes if using rolled oats).
Ladle into serving bowls. Drizzle each with maple syrup and finish with chopped toasted pecans for crunch.
5-minute-blender-hummus: Blend everything until nearly smooth, adding water gradually until you reach the texture you want.
Taste and adjust salt or lemon before serving.
oven-roasted-crispy-chickpeas: Dry the chickpeas thoroughly before roasting — this is what makes them crisp instead of soft.
Roast at 425°F/220°C for about 25-30 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through.
Season immediately after they come out of the oven, while still hot.
